label: Suspected Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda)
source: WHO / DRC Ministry of Health — DRC-Uganda Ebola, 25 May 2026
contestNote: 904 suspected cases; 101 lab-confirmed in DRC (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu) + 12 confirmed in Uganda (Kampala). Suspected count includes probable and unconfirmed deaths in conflict-inaccessible zones. 18 escaped ETU patients from Mongbwalu not fully traced.
deltaNote: Rapid surge from ~750 suspected cases on May 23 to 900+ by May 25 as outbreak expands to three DRC provinces

label: Lab-Confirmed Cases (2026 Outbreak — DRC + Uganda)
source: WHO / DRC MoH / Uganda MoH, 25 May 2026
deltaNote: 101 confirmed DRC + 12 confirmed Uganda (up from 85 DRC + 5 Uganda on May 23). Uganda cases jumped from 5 to 12 within 48 hours.

label: Suspected Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: WHO / DRC Ministry of Health, 25 May 2026
contestNote: 177+ suspected deaths across DRC; 10 confirmed deaths (9 DRC, 1 Uganda). Suspected figure includes community deaths in inaccessible zones of Ituri. Undercount likely. 18 escaped ETU patients from Mongbwalu represent additional untracked mortality risk.

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
contestNote: CFR ranges from 8.8% (10 confirmed deaths / 113 confirmed cases) to ~20% (177 suspected deaths / 900 suspected cases). BDBV historically 25–47% CFR in prior outbreaks; suspected community deaths are likely undercounted. ETU disruptions affect treatment access.

label: rVSV-ZEBOV Emergency Use Ring Vaccination
value: No licensed BDBV vaccine — Oxford 6–9 months
source: Oxford University / WHO IHR Emergency Committee, 22–25 May 2026
contestNote: rVSV-ZEBOV (Ervebo) licensed for Zaire ebolavirus only. Off-label ring vaccination ongoing. Oxford ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine is 6–9 months from Phase 1 human trials. MVA-BN-Filo BDBV on compassionate use. ETU attacks in Ituri have disrupted vaccination supply lines.
deltaNote: Oxford Jenner Institute confirmed timeline in statement released 22 May 2026; CEPI co-funding $45M for BDBV candidates
